equity_bridge.item: Non-current financial assets ex derivatives (incl. 19.85% TMICC stake at EUR 1.7bn fair value)
equity_bridge.note: AR FY2025 balance sheet 'Financial assets' (non-current) 3,065 less 140 of derivatives already netted in net debt. Includes the retained TMICC equity investment (EUR 1.7bn at 2025-12-31, to be sold down) and other equity investments. Their income ('Other income/(loss) from non-current investments' -17, TMICC fair-value movements through OCI) is outside EBITDA.

equity_bridge.item: Joint ventures and associates (Pepsi Lipton and others) at 12x FY2025 dividends
equity_bridge.note: Share of net profit of JVs and associates EUR 245m and dividends received EUR 243m (cash flow statement) are outside EBITDA; the stakes are carried within 'Other non-current assets' (976). Valued at 12x the EUR 243m cash dividend (~EUR 2.9bn), a mature-staples multiple; book value would be well under half this.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management USG guidance (4-6% multi-year, FY2026 'within' the range after the July 2026 raise, ~3% volume) less a structural ~0.5-1pp EUR translation drag, cross-checked against the 3-yr whole-company revenue CAGR of 5.0% and the owner-FCF CAGRs of 2.4-3.7%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 8.7% diverges >30% from revenue (3.2%) and EPS (1.4%): equity growth is retained earnings plus FX reserve movements on a stable business, not an operating growth signal, so it is NOT used as the growth source. Note too that the reported-FCF CAGRs (4.4%/2.8%) exceed the owner-FCF CAGRs (3.7%/2.4%) because SBC more than doubled from 151 to 324 over FY2019-FY2024.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs end at FY2024 (whole-company basis, FY2019-FY2024 on the pre-demerger perimeter) because FY2025 is continuing-operations only and not comparable: on the FY2025 filing's re-presented continuing basis turnover went 51,680 (FY2023) -> 52,479 (FY2024) -> 50,503 (FY2025), i.e. -3.8% reported in FY2025 on USG of +3.6% with a (5.9)% currency drag, and continuing diluted EPS 2.67 -> 2.44 -> 2.59. EPS is on the continuous post-consolidation share basis supplied by the parser. Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (interest received is outside OCF): 6,432 / 7,929 / 6,471 / 5,396 / 7,469 / 7,224 for FY2019-FY2024.

scenario_narratives.base: Volume-led 4% USG at the bottom of the range, ~1pp of structural EUR translation drag, UOM edging up from 20.0% with ~EUR 1bn/yr of restructuring treated as a real cost, Foods/McCormick RMT value-neutral. Pre-SBC EBITDA 21.1% -> 22.0% by FY2030; owner-FCF margin ~11% of turnover.
scenario_narratives.bull: US/India and premium Beauty bolt-ons lift USG to 5-6% with neutral FX; gross margin to 48-49% and restructuring fades post-separation; pre-SBC EBITDA 23.5%; focused HPC/Beauty Unilever earns a peer multiple (the re-rating is outside the flows).
scenario_narratives.bear: Subdued EM markets, 3-4pp EUR drag, private-label pressure, restructuring and separation costs persist, RMT delays, TMICC sold below carrying value; reported growth 0-2%, pre-SBC EBITDA 20.5%. Not a solvency case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unilever is valued as a mature, defensive compounder of owner free cash flow: statutory (not 'underlying') margins so that the EUR 1bn/yr of chronic restructuring is charged, SBC expensed with a flat share count, leases charged as operating cost, NCI leakage charged in the flows rather than deducted at book, and non-operating assets (TMICC stake, JV portfolio) added once in the bridge with the pension surplus conservatively ignored. Flows are EUR and discounted at a EUR WACC of 7%; per-share values are converted to pence at a dated, parity-checked rate. Terminal value is capped at 20x owner FCF in every scenario, so the valuation does not lean on a Gordon multiple above what a buyer pays for staples. The 15% hurdle entry price sits far below intrinsic value, as it must for a 7%-WACC asset growing 3%: the gap is the price of demanding 15% from a staple, not a model fault.
key_risks_to_valuation: EUR translation: 59% of turnover is emerging-market; each 1pp of sustained FX drag on reported growth is worth roughly 3-4% of value. The bear/base/bull growth spread is mostly FX, not USG.

Foods/McCormick RMT (close mid-2027): treated as value-neutral. Antitrust delay, a worse exchange ratio, stranded costs or a dis-synergy from losing Foods' scale in distribution would make it value-destructive; a successful pure-play re-rating is upside not in the flows.
Restructuring treated as permanent (~2pp of turnover). If Unilever genuinely stops restructuring after the Foods separation, pre-SBC EBITDA is ~1.5-2pp higher than base - roughly the bull margin.
Anchor vintage: net debt and share count are 2025-12-31; H1 2026 net debt was EUR 26.0bn (seasonal peak, buyback, M&A). Refresh both anchors together when the interim is extracted (~2.5% each way).
Terminal value is ~63-65% of EV at the 20x cap; a 15x exit (where Unilever has traded in weak years) would take ~20% off every scenario.
NCI leakage held at 8.5% of profit; HUL/Indonesia outgrowing the group raises leakage, bolt-ons in the US lower it.
Pension surplus (EUR 4.5bn gross, ~EUR 3.5bn net) excluded from the bridge: up to ~EUR 1.6/share of conservatism.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (ULVR.L) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3,644-5,542p. FX from Yahoo EURGBP=X on the same date; parity checked against UNA.AS (EUR) and UL (USD) closes.
data_sources.financials: research/ULVR.L/Reports/ULVR.L_Metrics.csv (FY2019-FY2025, EUR millions; FY2025 continuing operations) derived from core_metrics; component lines read from research/ULVR.L/Extracted/ULVR.L_Annual_FY2025.txt: income statement (l.9345-9377), cash flow statement (l.9585-9636), balance sheet (l.9516-9557), net debt reconciliation (l.2950-2968), note 7 share counts (l.10998-11004), note 10B leased assets (l.11350-11399), share capital (l.4455-4471).
data_sources.qualitative: research/ULVR.L/Reports/ULVR.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): business model, Power Brands, FY2026 guidance as raised at H1 2026, McCormick RMT terms, TMICC demerger, bull/bear cases.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2025-12-31 on the post-consolidation (8-for-9, 9 Dec 2025) basis: 2,181.0m shares in issue (AR FY2025 p.63, treasury effectively nil after the 10 Dec 2025 cancellation of 51.6m treasury shares; 0.3m held for share plans) plus 11.3m dilutive share-plan awards (FY2025 diluted 2,195.3m less basic 2,184.0m weighted average, note 7). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. The EUR 1.5bn 2026 buyback (tranche completed 5 Jun 2026) has since reduced the count by roughly 27m shares, but the cash left the balance sheet at the same time; both anchors are kept at the 2025-12-31 vintage for consistency.
inputs.sbc_source: AR FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement, 'Non-cash charge for share-based compensation' EUR 255m (continuing operations). Unilever settles awards from treasury shares; no separate equity-award tax line is disclosed, so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc (EquityAwardTaxes kpi recorded as 0).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 'Repurchase of shares' EUR 1,510m in financing activities (programme announced 13 Feb 2025, completed 30 May 2025). Repurchaser: the flat count is funded. A further EUR 1.5bn programme was announced Feb 2026 and ~EUR 6bn is targeted over 2026-2029; buybacks are value-neutral in this model (they are how the count stays flat).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in EUR; LSE quote in pence sterling (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 84.61 GBp per EUR = Yahoo EURGBP=X 0.8461 x 100, 2026-10-09T23:58Z. Parity check against the Amsterdam dual listing: UNA.AS EUR 55.30 (2026-10-09 close) x 84.61 = 4,679p vs the LSE close of 4,673.5p, a 0.1% tie confirming rate, direction and pence basis. The UL NYSE ADR (1 ADR = 1 share) at USD 62.26 is consistent at EURUSD ~1.126. Per-share values are computed in EUR and converted to GBp for the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv; EUR twins carry the _eur suffix.
inputs.anchor_vintage_note: FY2025 Annual Report (published 4 Mar 2026) is the latest filing in the Extracted folder; the H1 2026 interim (July 2026) has not been downloaded. The Analysis JSON reports H1 2026 net debt of EUR 26.0bn (2.3x UEBITDA) vs EUR 23.1bn at FY2025, reflecting the EUR 1.5bn buyback, bolt-on M&A (Dr. Squatch, Wild) and Unilever's normal H1 seasonal peak. Carrying the extra ~EUR 2.9bn of debt without the offsetting ~27m fewer shares and the acquired revenue would be inconsistent; each is worth roughly EUR 1.3/share (~2.5%), in opposite directions. Refresh both anchors together once the H1 2026 interim is extracted.
inputs.net_debt_definition: Unilever-defined net debt EUR 23,076m at 2025-12-31 (financial liabilities 2,582 + 25,696 = 28,278 less cash 3,941, other current financial assets 1,121 and non-current derivative assets 140), LESS lease liabilities of EUR 1,326m (note 15: 277 current + 1,049 non-current) because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B). total_debt 26,952 = 28,278 - 1,326; cash 5,202 = 3,941 + 1,121 + 140. Non-current financial assets other than the 140 of derivatives sit in equity_bridge, not here.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-denominated flows discounted at a EUR-built WACC of 7.0%: 10y Bund ~2.7% (Oct 2026) + 5.3% ERP x beta 1.0 = 8.0% cost of equity (observed beta ~0.5 would give ~5.4%, which the house does not use for a 59%-emerging-market earner); pre-tax cost of debt ~3.8% (A+/A1, EUR bonds), 2.8% after tax; D/(D+E) ~18% at market -> 7.1%, rounded to 7.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, FX and execution risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) - leases as operating cost. The full lease cash cost (capital element EUR 301m in financing + interest on leases EUR 79m = EUR 380m total cash outflow, note 10B) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (0.75% of turnover), lease liabilities (EUR 1,326m) are EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (1,353 - 367 = 986, 1.95% of turnover) so the lease is not charged twice. ebitda_margin_path is pre-SBC statutory EBITDA (operating profit 9,037 + D&A 1,353 + SBC 255 = 10,645, 21.1%); FY0 tie-out: 21.1 - 0.5 SBC - 0.75 lease - 1.95 D&A = 17.9% EBIT = EUR 9,030m vs reported 9,037 adjusted for the lease swap (9,037 - 79 lease interest + 367 ROU depreciation - 301 principal = 9,024).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the flows: cash_tax_rate_path is a combined tax-plus-NCI leakage rate. Cash tax ~27% of EBIT (underlying ETR 25.7%, statutory 29.4%, cash paid 31% of PBT in FY2025 inflated by Ice Cream separation taxes) and NCI 8.5% of continuing net profit (531 / 6,213; Hindustan Unilever ~38% minority, Unilever Indonesia, Pakistan, Nigeria) combine to 1 - 0.73 x 0.915 = 33.2%, used as 33%. Calibration: FY0 EBIT 9,030 x 0.67 = 6,050 vs attributable continuing profit 5,682 + after-tax net finance cost 503 x 0.73 = 6,049. The EUR 2,057m NCI book value is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge (that would be the double count), and market value of the minorities (HUL alone ~EUR 20bn+) is irrelevant because their share of the flows never reaches the valuation.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2: non-US operating company, consumer staples, EUR filer with a GBp quote), with the adaptations for currency (a1/a2), leases (b), NCI (c) and excluded income (d). Not cyclical or distressed. Fresh build - no prior DCF, no MEMORY entry. BASIS: FY2025 continuing operations (ex Ice Cream, demerged 6 Dec 2025 as TMICC) for turnover, EBITDA, D&A, capex, SBC, tax; statutory NetIncome 9,469 includes the EUR 3,373m demerger gain and EUR 425m of discontinued profit, so the attributable anchor is NetIncomeContinuing 5,682 (kpis). The pending Foods/McCormick Reverse Morris Trust (announced 31 Mar 2026, EV ~USD 44.8bn, close mid-2027, Unilever receives ~USD 15.7bn cash and shareholders receive 55.1% of the combined MKC plus a 9.9% direct Unilever stake) is a repackaging of value already inside the modelled flows: Foods (~26% of turnover) is valued here as a continuing Unilever business, and the deal is treated as approximately value-neutral at first order rather than modelled as deal-completes/deal-breaks. It is not a takeover of Unilever, so the three-scenario frame stands; the re-rating argument for a pure-play HPC/Beauty Unilever is part of the bull narrative, and antitrust/stranded-cost/governance risk is part of the bear. last_fcf follows the contract (reported FCF 6,461 - SBC 255 - interest income 0 = 6,206): finance income (EUR 398m) is excluded from EBITDA and 'Interest received' sits in investing activities, so it was never inside OCF and no deduction is needed; the cash it earns is netted in net debt. The component build additionally charges lease cash (0.75%) and NCI leakage, so projected year-1 owner FCF (~EUR 5.7bn, 11.0% of turnover) is deliberately below last_fcf; FY2025 OCF also carried ~EUR 0.3bn of separation-related taxes and a +116 working-capital inflow grossed up by the TMICC transitional services arrangement. Working capital: Unilever runs structurally negative working capital (payables 16.9bn vs inventories 4.0bn + receivables 7.3bn), so growth releases cash; wc_capture_pct is held at 0 as the conservative choice. SBC-light market: SBC is 0.5% of turnover, so house and street bases are close but not identical (band_position is meaningful but narrow). EXCLUDED INCOME / MATCHING ASSETS (rule d): share of JV/associate profit (245) and other investment income are outside EBITDA, so the JV portfolio and non-current financial assets go in equity_bridge; the EUR 123m pension finance income is also excluded but the EUR 4.5bn pension surplus is deliberately NOT added (trapped surplus, refund tax, deficits of 944 on other schemes) - a conservative omission worth up to ~EUR 1.6/share.

bear.narrative: Markets stay subdued, Latin America and Indonesia keep resetting, and a persistent 3-4pp EUR translation drag (the FY2025 drag was 5.9pp) holds reported growth near 0-2% even with USG of 3-4%. Private label and retailer pressure in Europe and the US cap pricing, so gross-margin gains are reinvested in brand support rather than dropping through; restructuring and Foods separation/stranded costs stay at ~EUR 1bn+ a year and pre-SBC EBITDA slips to 20.5%. The McCormick RMT runs into antitrust delay or a weaker exchange ratio, the TMICC stake is sold down below carrying value, and net debt stays around 2.3x UEBITDA, leaving less room for the EUR 6bn buyback programme. No solvency dimension: A+/A1 balance sheet, ~100% cash conversion. Terminal growth 2.0%; Gordon (20.4x) and cap (20x) nearly coincide.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 reported +2.5%: USG ~4.5% (guidance 'within' 4-6% after Q2 USG of 5.8%, H2 guided 4-5%) less ~2.5pp EUR translation drag at current EUR strength, plus ~0.5pp net M&A (Dr. Squatch, Wild, Minimalist less Conimex/Vegetarian Butcher/REN disposals). FY2027-FY2030 +3.5%: USG at the 4% bottom of the range with the structural ~0.5pp FX drag of a 59%-emerging-market earner reporting in EUR. Taper to 2.5% terminal (nominal EUR, below long-run nominal GDP).
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC statutory EBITDA 21.1% in FY2025 (UOM 20.0% + D&A 2.6% = UEBITDA 22.6%, less ~2.1pp of chronic restructuring and other non-underlying items, EUR 1,047m, which Unilever books every year and are treated here as a real cost). Guidance is 'modest improvement' in UOM; base lifts 20bps a year to 22.0% by FY2030 (gross margin 46.9% and rising on productivity/mix; restructuring stays) and holds. Capex 3.1% of turnover (FY2025 PPE 1,417 + intangibles 174 = 3.15%) easing to 3.0%; D&A ex-ROU 2.0% (1.95% FY2025); lease cash 0.75%; SBC flat 0.5%; combined tax+NCI leakage 33% (see nci_treatment).
base.narrative: Unilever executes the volume-led algorithm it has delivered for 12 straight quarters - 4% USG at the bottom of its range, ~2-3% from volume, gross margin grinding higher on SKU cuts and productivity - but EUR reporting against emerging-market currencies keeps reported growth a point or more below USG, and ~EUR 1bn/yr of restructuring persists through the Foods separation and the post-TMICC stranded-cost clean-up. The Foods/McCormick RMT closes mid-2027 and is roughly value-neutral to today's shareholder. Terminal value at the 20x cap (Gordon at 7%/2.5% would be 22.8x).

bull.narrative: The US and India anchor markets keep outgrowing, premium Beauty & Wellbeing bolt-ons (Dr. Squatch, Nutrafol, Liquid I.V., Wild, Minimalist) compound at double digits, and USG runs at 5-6% with FX neutral-to-helpful as EM currencies stabilise. Gross margin pushes toward 48-49% and the restructuring burden fades after the Foods separation, so pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 23.5% (UOM ~22%). The RMT delivers a focused ~EUR 39bn HPC/Beauty company that the market re-rates toward P&G/Colgate multiples - the re-rating itself is not in these flows, only the better margins and growth it would rest on. Terminal growth 3.0%, cap 20x binds (Gordon 25.8x).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bull weight DOWN because the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once - sustained 5%+ USG that Unilever has delivered in only two of the last ten years, neutral EM currencies, a clean Foods separation and a fading restructuring charge - and the pure-play re-rating is a multiple argument, not a cash-flow one. Bear weight UP (not to 35%) because the bear is a familiar Unilever pattern (FX drag, Latin America, chronic restructuring, portfolio churn, governance friction over an un-voted RMT) rather than solvency or covenant risk: A+/A1 credit, 2.0-2.3x leverage, 100% cash conversion. Base 50%: the FY2026 guidance raise in July shows the volume algorithm is working, but 'markets will likely remain subdued' is management's own framing.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
